title: Threshold repetition for entangled games
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that for every finite two-player one-round game with entangled value v < 1, the probability of winning at least a fraction v + delta of k parallel repetitions decays exponentially in k, uniformly over all finite-dimensional entangled strategies. A universal rate proportional to delta^5/(1 + log d) rests on a conditioning estimate of Song, a named hypothesis of the course; a rate proportional to delta^3, with a constant depending on the question distribution, is proved in full. The first lesson defines games, strategies and repetition, states the theorems and the named hypothesis, and proves that each coordinate is won with probability at most v. The second proves the transfer from conditioning estimates to threshold bounds by sampling tested coordinates and taking tensor copies, deduces the universal theorem, and derives two-sided error amplification. The third constructs the resolvent purification of effects, proves its operator entropy estimate, and transports answer measurements with exact probabilities. The fourth builds, for each untested coordinate, conditional vectors and local measurements that reproduce the conditional answers, and bounds their one-question approximations by an entropy telescope; it also bounds the drift of the question law. The fifth replaces the vectors by one reference vector on each component of the question support, obtains legal one-game strategies, proves a conditioning estimate with square-root error and the cubic threshold bound.
prerequisites: course The Gaussian moat problem, lesson Entropy of finite random variables: chain rule and conditioning for entropy (Propositions 2.2 and 2.3), relative entropy and total variation (Definition 5.1), Pinsker's inequality (Theorem 5.3)
course The Gaussian moat problem, lesson Concentration and the discrete cube: Hoeffding's inequality (Theorem 2.2)
finite-dimensional linear algebra: the spectral theorem for self-adjoint matrices, positive operators, tensor products
the named hypothesis (S) of the first lesson, used only for the universal fifth-power theorem and the soundness half of the amplification corollary; the lessons prove every other fact they use

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (S): Song's conditioning estimate (ECCC TR26-199, Definition 4.3 and Lemma 4.4); its proof uses smooth correlated sampling and Lemmas 3.1-3.3 of Chapter 6 of OpenAI's Ten Advances report as black boxes. Not proved in the programme; only the universal fifth-power theorem and the soundness half of the amplification corollary depend on it. The cubic theorem is proved in full.

Missing foundation: a course on quantum parallel repetition (Chapter 6 of OpenAI's Ten Advances report: greedy conditioning, the ideal conditioned state, quantum correlated sampling) together with Song's smooth sampler would close (S).
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
